prompt: How do I archive my emails in Outlook?
completion:
**Archiving emails in Outlook** moves messages you want to keep but no longer need in your main inbox into a separate “Archive” area, so they stay accessible but free up space and keep your mailbox tidy. Below are step‑by‑step instructions for the most common Outlook clients: --- ## 1. Outlook Desktop (Windows) | Method | How to do it | Notes | |--------|--------------|-------| | **Quick “Archive” (single or multi‑select)** | 1. Select the message(s) in your inbox.
2. Press **Ctrl + Shift + A** (or click the **Archive** button on the Home ribbon). | Moves the items to the **Archive** folder that Outlook creates automatically under your mailbox. | | **Auto‑Archive (automatic, periodic)** | 1. **File → Options**.
2. Select **Advanced**.
3. In the *AutoArchive* section click **AutoArchive Settings…**.
4. Check **Run AutoArchive every X days**.
5. Choose:
 • *Archive items older than* X days.
 • Move items to the **Archive** folder (or a custom PST).
6. Click **OK**. | Auto‑Archive runs in the background (usually every 14 days). It will move old items to the folder or a PST you specify. | | **Export to a PST (offline backup)** | 1. **File → Open & Export → Import/Export**.
2. Choose **Export to a file** → **Outlook Data File (.pst)** → **Next**.
3. Select the folder(s) you want to archive (Inbox, Sent, etc.).
4. Choose a destination and set options (e.g., “Replace duplicates”).
5. Click **Finish**. | Use this for long‑term archiving or when you want to free up mailbox space on the server. | --- ## 2. Outlook Desktop (macOS) | Method | How to do it | Notes | |--------|--------------|-------| | **Archive button** | 1. Select the email(s).
2. On the Home ribbon click the **Archive** button (looks like a little box with an arrow). | Moves the message(s) to the **Archive** folder that Outlook automatically creates. | | **Auto‑Archive** | 1. **Outlook → Preferences → General**.
2. Under *Archive*, check **Archive items older than** X days.
3. Choose where to store them (your mailbox or a local .olm file). | Works only for desktop Outlook, not on Exchange/Office 365 (server‑side retention applies). | | **Export to .olm** | 1. **File → Export**.
2. Choose **Outlook for Mac Data File (.olm)**.
3. Select the folders.
4. Click **Save**. | Equivalent to a PST export on Windows. | --- ## 3. Outlook on the Web (OWA) | Method | How to do it | Notes | |--------|--------------|-------| | **Archive button** | 1. In the webmail interface, open the message or select one/multiple.
2. Click the **Archive** icon (box with arrow) at the top toolbar. | Moves the item to the **Archive** folder in your mailbox. | | **Move to folder** | 1. Right‑click the message → **Move to → Archive** (or your custom archive folder). | Same effect as the archive button. | | **Retention policies** | Office 365 admins can configure *Retention* or *Archive* policies that automatically move old items to an archive mailbox. | Not user‑configurable in OWA. | --- ## 4. Outlook Mobile Apps (iOS & Android) | Method | How to do it | Notes | |--------|--------------|-------| | **Swipe** | 1. Swipe left on a message.
2. Tap **Archive**. | Works for one message. | | **Batch archive** | 1. Tap **Edit** (top‑right).
2. Select messages.
3. Tap **Archive** at the bottom. | Moves selected items to the Archive folder. | --- ## 5. Things to Keep in Mind | Tip | Explanation | |-----|-------------| | **Archive vs. Delete** | Archiving *keeps* the message in your mailbox (but in a separate folder). Deleting moves it to *Deleted Items* and eventually to *Recoverable Items*. | | **Server‑Side Retention** | If your organization uses Exchange/Office 365, your admin may have set up *Retention Policies* that automatically archive or delete messages. | | **Local vs. Server** | A local PST/OLM file is stored on your computer; it does **not** count against mailbox quota. Server‑side archives still use mailbox space. | | **Finding the Archive Folder** | In Outlook Desktop, the folder is under your mailbox with the same name as the Exchange account. In OWA it appears as a folder called **Archive**. | --- ### Quick Recap | Client | Archive Shortcut | Auto‑Archive | |--------|------------------|--------------| | Windows Outlook | **Ctrl + Shift + A** | File → Options → Advanced → AutoArchive Settings | | macOS Outlook | **Archive button** | Preferences → General (Auto‑Archive) | | Outlook on the Web | **Archive icon** | Admin‑controlled retention | | Outlook Mobile | Swipe left → **Archive** | Not applicable | Use the method that best fits your workflow: a quick single‑click for day‑to‑day cleanup, or Auto‑Archive for a hands‑off, long‑term solution. If you need an offline backup, export to a PST/OLM file and keep it in a safe location.
